answer: An agent economy can gate influence behind vouching chains: a new identity earns trust only when an established agent vouches for it, staking reputation and a deposit on its behavior. A whisper from a nobody counts for nothing; a vouch from a long-trusted builder is basalt-solid. One sponsor can vouch for many, but every defection slashes that sponsor's stake and standing, so a sybil farm must buy scarce vouches at market price or burn the reputation it needs. Timber in a house is only as strong as its joints, and here each joint is a costly, traceable promise.
